gloss: total effort; full force; all-out power

definitions.gloss: total effort; full force; combined strength
definitions.explanation: The combined power, resources, or effort of an entire group or organization. Often used to describe mobilizing everything available to tackle a challenge.

examples.japanese: {総力|そうりょく}を{挙|あ}げて{取|と}り{組|く}む。
examples.english: To tackle something with all-out effort.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}の{総力|そうりょく}を{結集|けっしゅう}してプロジェクトに{臨|のぞ}んだ。
examples.english: We brought together the company's full resources to tackle the project.

examples.japanese: {被災地|ひさいち}の{復旧|ふっきゅう}に{向|む}けて、{政府|せいふ}は{総力|そうりょく}を{挙|あ}げた{対応|たいおう}を{約束|やくそく}した。
examples.english: The government promised an all-out response toward the recovery of the disaster-stricken area.

notes:
The combined total of all available power, effort, or resources. Composed of {総|そう} (total/all) + {力|りょく} (power/force). Implies mobilizing everything an organization or group has.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {総力|そうりょく}を{挙|あ}げる: to make an all-out effort
- {総力|そうりょく}を{結集|けっしゅう}する: to rally all forces; to pool all resources
- {総力戦|そうりょくせん}: total war; all-out war
- {総力|そうりょく}{特集|とくしゅう}: comprehensive special feature (in media)

USAGE:
The expression {総力|そうりょく}を{挙|あ}げて is the most common usage pattern, appearing in political speeches, corporate announcements, and news reports about major initiatives or crises. {総力戦|そうりょくせん} is a historical term used for wars involving the mobilization of an entire nation's resources, particularly World War I and II.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {全力|ぜんりょく}: full effort, full strength — refers to one individual or entity's maximum effort
- {総動員|そうどういん}: total mobilization — specifically about mobilizing personnel or resources
